name: Adrenaline Rush

date.source: The fed's own title date, 12-28-08, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 29 December 2008.

appearances.note: Rushed the ring immediately after Sonny Williams retained the Intercontinental Championship and beat him bloody with bare fists until security and referees pulled him off; later stood on the ramp on Brian Michaels' side when the whole roster emptied out for the main events.

notes: The fed's own championship ledger bills this show "Adrenaline Rush II". This show crowns D.C. as MWE's first Undisputed Champion via a Three Stages of Hell unification match against Brian Michaels. It also stages what its own text presents as two distinct MWE Tag Team Championships in play the same night (Project Revolution winning one via a chaotic three-team Triple Tag scramble; Darius & Boyd retaining the other against the Hollywood Hooligans) — resolved two shows later on the 12 January 2009 Monday Night Mayhem, whose own text explicitly unifies "both sets of Tag Team Titles" via a match between the two respective champion teams.

matches.note: For the Havok Championship (new champion). Milenko's stablemates The Wraith and The Ringmaster (neither registered) accompanied him and interfered, including spraying JJ Executioner in the face with a fire extinguisher.
X-TV Championship tournament final. Mysterious G unmasked after winning, revealing Eric Derf.

Billed as a Triple Tag Team match for the MWE Tag Team Titles between three teams: Grand Mystique & Maxximillion Mustafa, Triple Threat (Milenko's stablemates The Wraith and The Ringmaster, neither registered), and Project Revolution. Grand Mystique attacked his own partner Maxx before the bell (see angle appearances) and never functioned as a competing side; The Wraith and Ringmaster (unregistered) brawled with Project Revolution, who pinned The Wraith to win the titles. Neither Grand Mystique nor Maxximillion Mustafa is included here since neither functioned as an actual combatant in the resolution (see the show's angle appearances instead).

For the Intercontinental Championship (Sonny Williams retains). The third entrant is announced as "the SUPERNOVA, Vega Knight" but is called only "Supernova"/"Nova" throughout the match commentary — MWE's own roster separately has a distinct registered character named Supernova; flagged as a genuine ambiguity rather than force-resolved (see flags).
For the MWE Tag Team Championships (Darius & Boyd retain).

Originally ruled a draw when neither man answered the referee's ten count; Richard Covell restarted the match immediately as No Disqualification (second bell), and Joey Dallas won via a ten count after driving Cannon off the entrance stage through a table with the Damnation.

Fall one of a Three Stages of Hell match billed as unifying the MWE World Heavyweight Championship (Michaels) and MWE Heavyweight Championship (D.C.) for the first Undisputed Championship. Guest ring announcer Michael Buffer (the real-world boxing/wrestling announcer) introduced this fall; not entered in appearances (see flags).
Fall two of the same Three Stages of Hell unification match.
Fall three of the same Three Stages of Hell unification match; D.C. won the series 2-1 to become MWE's first Undisputed Champion.

The show refers to itself in its own closing line as "Crowning Glory III" and opening commentary calls it a "2 Year Anniversary" show ("Two years are gone") -- continuity data points, see flags. Zack Crash becomes X-TV Champion, Grand Mystique becomes World Heavyweight Champion; Mason Resoan retains the United States Championship. Eric Derf wins the inaugural Money in the Bank match. A Chris England vs. Leon Roberts match billed for this show never formally started -- see the match-2 area and flags. WcE's JEST'ers -- James Whitman, Eddie Sanchez, Scott Jones and Thomas Williams -- walk out as a four-man act before the Whitman/Rodriguez retirement match, have Ryan Adams and David Ferrera ejected from the announce desk on GM Eli Silver's say-so, and run the broadcast for that match themselves: Whitman, Sanchez and MWE's own Darrel Jones on commentary, Jones and Williams on the cameras, Billy Joe Barker on the bell. Adams and Ferrera are back for the main event. The unit and its three unregistered members were minted on 2026-09-02.

Grand Mystique wins (Super Big Bang) to become the new MWE World Heavyweight Champion; post-match, he assaulted the outgoing champion with a second Big Bang and a Hand of Prophecy through two chairs.

name: Friday Night Genesis

date.source: The fed's own title date, 12-12-08, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 13 December 2008.

notes: The last-ever edition of Friday Night Genesis; GM Dick Malibu states on-air that the brand is being cancelled without his input ("to take MY show off the air without even consulting me is down right bullls***"). Both titles minted on the prior Genesis episode change hands here: the World Tag Team Championship (Ace Cannon & Joey Dallas defeat Maxxamillion Mustafa & The Grand Mystique) and the Intercontinental Championship (Sonny Williams defeats Vega Knight). Announcer Stasiak quits on air mid-show over a disagreement with broadcast partner Jacobs, leaving Jacobs to call the main event alone (joined at ringside by guest commentator Brian Michaels). Paige returns from an unexplained absence to help D.C. defeat Leon "The Virus" Roberts in the non-title main event. Brian Michaels confirms the D.C. vs Michaels Adrenaline Rush match is a Three Stages of Hell bout, corroborating the stipulation named on the mnm-2008-12-01 pre-show card. Cannon and Dallas, freshly co-champions, immediately brawl; GM Dick Malibu threatens to void both contracts if either touches the other again before their own Adrenaline Rush match.

notes: Friday Night Genesis's debut episode under new general manager Dick Malibu, following the Draft. Because the World Heavyweight, Tag Team and X-TV Championships stayed exclusive to Monday Night Mayhem, Genesis crowns its own brand-exclusive "MWE World Heavyweight Championship" via an in-show tournament (won by D.C. in the Steel Cage main event) and hands Maxxamillion Mustafa & The Grand Mystique a new "MWE World Tag Team Championship" and Vega Knight a new Genesis Intercontinental title, replacing the belts they held on Mayhem. Commentary explicitly frames Genesis as "the continuation of the EW legacy that we once thought was lost," and GM Dick Malibu recaps EW's collapse ("EW died because a great man let his inmates run the asylum"). Brian Michaels closes the show promising new champion D.C. a challenger, "the Virus," teased with the date 12-12-08 — matching the debut of Leon Roberts (registered as "The Virus") on the Friday Night Genesis show of that date, also in this batch.

date.source: The fed's own title date, 03-29-09, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 29 March 2009.

notes: Opens on Sinc Mercier's return promo. Vanguard then beats down D.C. and superkicks his pregnant partner Tera (referred to in-text as 'Tera Jean Star' — see flags on the Tera McQueen near-miss). Paige becomes the first woman to hold the MWE Intercontinental Championship. Post-main-event, David Whitman celebrates with Brian Michaels and Blood Fuze (Triple G, Mr. Markowitz) as 'the new Mayhem Mafia' — the show's own text explicitly calls this 'nu-MWE' (Triple G and Markowitz's 'first tag team victory in nu-MWE').

MWE's own memorial show for founder Tim Fitzgerald: a full-roster ten-bell salute opens the show, with tribute speeches from Alejandro Rodriguez, Jesse "Semi" Anderson, D.C., and visiting guests from Illinois Championship Wrestling, Wrestle Crazy Entertainment, and Wrestling's Highest Quality. The ring announcer calls thirteen men into the ring by name for the tribute segment: four of MWE's own, five billed for Wrestle Crazy Entertainment (James Whitman, Lennox Armstrong, Mark Marvin, Adam Belmont, Ken Forte) and four for Wrestling's Highest Quality (Jesse "Semi" Anderson, Jack Savage, Dylan Duncan, Krauser); Mark Marvin and James Whitman speak on camera. The nine visitors were minted under their own wings on 2026-09-02 and carry angle appearances here. D.C.'s eulogy explicitly frames the promotion's relaunch as continuous with the original ("this fed was brought back to life, because people missed being home") — see flags, continuity. A new masked stable calling itself "the Saintz" (three men plus one woman, no names given) debuts in a cold-open vignette (see flags, mint-candidate).

Ended in a disqualification when Paige — pulled from her own scheduled match on this card — attacked Warner from behind and stole the title belt; Grand Mystique then Big Banged Warner as well, suggesting an alliance with Paige despite losing the match to her interference.
Brothers' rivalry match (see mwe-mnm-2009-01-26's own notes on the Covell family reveal).
Non-title main event; both men wore "TF" armbands in tribute and shook hands before and after the match. Alejandro Rodriguez's second win over Whitman in as many weeks.

name: Tribulation

date.source: The fed's own title date, 05-24-09, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 24 May 2009.

notes: Supercard, multiple title changes. Order 1 (Scavenger Hunt) UNIFIES the United States and Intercontinental Championships under Sinc Mercier ('new Unified United States and Intercontinental Champion') — worth a titles.json note; post-match Sinc is attacked by Windy Bridges and an unregistered run-in, Nate Rellington (see flags). Order 2 is a Fatal Four-Way #1-contendership match for the X-Television Championship; 'Sin' (unregistered, recurring across two shows now — see flags) is omitted from participants[]. Order 4: Nic Kraven wins the vacant X-Television Championship from Eric Derf. Order 6 (D.C. vs Kevin Hardaway, Last Man Standing) has an unregistered opponent (Hardaway) so the row carries only D.C., who is also the winner (winner_side: 0 is truthful here since the registered entrant won). Zak Warner's #1-contendership match is forfeited on-air to Joseph Sharpman (a kayfabe drug-test suspension); Sharpman then cuts a promo and QUITS MWE on the broadcast — no in-ring contest occurred, so no matches[] row was written for the forfeit itself, only Sharpman's angle appearance. Order 7 is a Steel Cage match. Richard Covell then inducts the MWE Hall of Fame Class of 2009 on camera — Paige, Sonny Williams, Alejandro Rodriguez, and Brian Michaels — with Michaels and Rodriguez both announcing in-story retirements effective at a future show, 'Crowning Glory.' This Hall of Fame induction likely needs its own registry treatment (halloffame.json or similar) beyond what this appearances pass covers. Main event (order 8) is billed non-title even though Whitman is reigning World Champion, since Semi surrendered his own title (the X-TV strap) rather than putting a title on the line — see the prior show's notes for that surrender.

name: Turmoil

date.source: The fed's own title date, 9-14-08, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 15 September 2008.

notes: MWE's first three-way Tag Team Championship match (won by Project Revolution over the Hollywood Hooligans and the Bowens, the latter billed here as "Burning Legion"); Sinc Mercier becomes the new United States Champion; Brian Michaels vs. D.C. ends in a double Ace-of-Spades double-knockout no-contest; Sonny Williams becomes the new World Heavyweight Champion in a triple threat over Jekyl and David Whitman, and Jekyl's post-match rampage against Sonny (a ladder dive through the announce table, a knife pulled at ringside) ends with Jekyl arrested and led out in handcuffs.

name: Turmoil

date.source: The fed's own title date, 10-25-09, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 25 October 2009.

notes: CSB defeated Grand Mystique in a First Blood match to become the new MWE Undisputed Champion; immediately after, Kevin Hardaway (revealed wearing a GWC shirt) turned on CSB with a Williams Driver, draping the shirt and the newly-won title over him. Sinc Mercier announced his retirement, was interrupted by Zak Warner, and Eli Silver booked them for a No Holds Barred match at the next Monday Night Mayhem. Leon Roberts retained the MWE United States Championship in a three-way billed as "TLC" but staged purely as a ladder match, against Zak Warner and Brad Kane (unresolved, omitted from matches[]). Eli Silver announced a future Team MWE (Alexis Black, Eric Derf, D.C., Sinc Mercier, Grand Mystique) vs Team GWC (Leon Roberts, Zak Warner, CSB, Kevin Hardaway, Zack Crash) 5-on-5 elimination tag match, prompted by a call from former GWC owner Danny Vice; a brawl broke out among the assembled rosters when the teams were revealed. CSB also revealed a GWC World Heavyweight Championship belt during his opening promo, establishing his own prior GWC background.

name: Wrestle-Wars

date.source: The fed's own title date, 10-26-08, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 26 October 2008.

notes: The fed's own championship ledger bills this show "Wrestle Wars II". A title-heavy supercard: the X-TV Championship is retained by Vega Knight, the Tag Team Championship changes to Maxxamillion Mustafa & The Grand Mystique, the United States Championship changes to Alejandro Rodriguez, and the World Heavyweight Championship changes to David Whitman (his third reign). The Alex Bowen/Milenko Hardcore match is ruled a draw mid-match after an unforeseen incident (an errant Tempest crashing into the pyrotechnics setup), then restarted at Richard Covell's order and finished decisively for Milenko — recorded here as a single match row (order 3) per the two-bells-one-match convention rather than two rows. Post-match, Alejandro Rodriguez is nearly run over in the parking lot; the driver is revealed to be Mason Resoan, and Billy Joe Barker (a production-crew member) saves him, leading Alejandro to offer to help him become a wrestler. Richard Covell closes the show announcing a Draft making all MWE talent eligible, foreshadowing the Nov 10 Draft Special. Ace Cannon's debut promo asserts explicit year-over-year continuity for MWE ("the same tired talent that was MWE over a year ago... the same old sh*t just the calendar reads 2008 and not 2007").

name: Wrestle Wars

date.source: The fed's own title date, 12-6-09, read MM-DD-YY per MWE's own dating convention; posted to the fed's own board 6 December 2009.

notes: Blight defeated Josh Parker (unresolved, omitted from matches[]) in a Barbed Wire Rope match. Alexis Black and Madison Seton's Team MWE decider ended in a mutual double-knockout after both used weapons simultaneously; Eli Silver retroactively declared it a Loser Is Fired match and released both from the roster. Ace Cannon won a No Rules fatal four-way for a shot at the XTV title. Oblivion won the vacated XTV Championship in a High Road triple threat over Zack Crash and Scotty McKnight, then unmasked and declared himself "Supernova Vega Knight" — the roster carries both "Supernova" and "Vega Knight" as separate entities with no aka cross-reference, so this reveal is not resolved to either id (see flags). Zak Warner won the MWE United States Championship from The Virus (Leon Roberts) in a Shattered Glass match, then assaulted Sinc Mercier backstage. CSB retained the MWE World Heavyweight Championship over D.C. with Sinc Mercier as special guest referee. A final, out-of-sequence segment stages Eric Derf against a newly-recast, explicitly first-time-appearing masked "Grand Mystique" ("no matter who is under that mask now" — Ferrera; "I don't want to know where he came from or even who he is" — Ferrera post-match) who wins with a new finisher ("The Darkness"); this performer is not resolved to the-grand-mystique-mwe, who is not otherwise booked on this card despite being MWE's reigning-champion-turned-challenger storyline anchor going into it (see flags).

name: Independence Day 2007

evidence.note: Ryan Adams' own staff entry credits him with calling "the infamous Mason Resoan vs D.C. vs Aiden Copane vs Pala match at Independence Day 2007" — a named match on a named card of the original run.
MWE staged Independence Day again on 5 July 2009, which is held; the 2007 card is the series' own earlier staging.

notes: Staged during the original MWE run, whose board (z4.invisionfree.com/MWEntertainment) survives in the Wayback Machine as four homepage captures and no thread of any kind.

name: Crowning Glory I

date.source: Undated in the surviving record. The original MWE ran from 2007 until 20 March 2008, and its successor staged Crowning Glory II on 10 August 2008 and a third the following August, which places the first staging inside the original run.

evidence.note: A roleplay of 31 August 2008 stages a character in an entertainment store reading "the blurb in the back of the video of Crowning Glory I" — the fed's own in-fiction record of an earlier Crowning Glory.
A May 2009 roleplay written as a fan letter to Brian Michaels dates his own promo record "from your Crowning Glory I promo" onward.
The relaunch's own August 2008 supershow is billed Crowning Glory II on the show document itself and in the fed's own championship ledger.

notes: The first staging of the fed's flagship pay-per-view, on the original MWE board; the second and third stagings are held.

name: MWE's first show (2007)

date.source: Undated beyond the year in the surviving record. The original MWE ran from 2007 until 20 March 2008, and the fed's own 2009 Hall of Fame retrospective situates a Sonny Williams vs John Austin match on this card as the fed's own first show.

evidence.note: The fed's own 24 May 2009 Hall of Fame induction segment: Richard Covell inducts Sonny Williams as "the ONLY superstar in MWE history to go from facing John Austin to David Whitman", immediately followed by "The memories from MWE's first show pour in, and Covell begins to tear up" — the fed's own record situating a Sonny Williams vs John Austin match on its own first card of the original 2007 run.

notes: Staged during the original MWE run, whose board (z4.invisionfree.com/MWEntertainment) survives in the Wayback Machine as four homepage captures and no thread of any kind — the same gap mwe-independence-day-2007 and mwe-crowning-glory-i record. The Hall of Fame speech names neither of those cards, so this is filed as a distinct, unnamed card rather than folded into either.
